statement: Let m = len(mat) and n = len(mat[0]). A valid cell sequence of length k is a sequence of cell indices (i_0,j_0),...,(i_{k-1},j_{k-1}) such that 0 <= i_t < m and 0 <= j_t < n for every t, and for every t with 0 <= t < k-1, (i_t = i_{t+1} or j_t = j_{t+1}) and mat[i_t][j_t] < mat[i_{t+1}][j_{t+1}]. A single cell is a valid sequence of length 1. Let L be the largest k for which a valid cell sequence of length k exists. Whenever the function returns a result r, r = L.
preconditions: Let m = len(mat) and n = len(mat[0]). The matrix is non-empty and rectangular: 1 <= m <= 100000, 1 <= n <= 100000, every row of mat has length n, m*n <= 100000, and every entry mat[i][j] with 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n satisfies -100000 <= mat[i][j] <= 100000.
